claims.text: ADR 0015 keeps the invoice signing key in an HSM only Payments may call; ADR 0023 puts that HSM in the provider's HSM service; ADR 0022 runs production on managed Kubernetes; bank-signing-requirements.md does not reopen them.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/bank-signing-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 10-12; docs/adr/0015 Quyết định; docs/adr/0023 Quyết định

claims.text: The bank owns a chain of shops on Đơn Hàng and is the customer of compliance-controls.md; it wants each month a statement of its shops' payments and refunds, signed by Payments.
A certificate is valid only between two dates written in it; certificate revocation is its issuing CA declaring it invalid before the end date, for example because its private key may have leaked.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/bank-signing-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 18-20; .NET API docs X509Certificate2.NotBefore / NotAfter; content/glossary.yaml certificate-revocation

claims.text: KS-1 bank checks alone with public key and certificate, no call to Đơn Hàng; KS-2 checkable after expiry, knowing when signed, 10 years (assumed); KS-3 signed before revocation valid, after not; KS-4 key never leaves HSM; KS-5 each signing request logged outside Payments' tables.
The bank's controls reuse compliance-controls.md: KS-4 is TT-3, KS-5 is TT-2, separation of duties between approver and maker is TT-1, review of who may sign and administer keys is TT-7.

Estimate: at most a few hundred statements a month (assumed, one per shop); signing load negligible; a statement may wait a few hours (assumed) if ready by the bank's deadline, the fifth working day of the next month (assumed); the hard part is time, not load.

Assumptions, none confirmed yet, with who is to confirm: the bank trusts only roots it names, the certificate from a CA it names (product owner, asking the bank); 10 years (product owner with accounting); no HSM on own machines demanded (product owner); deadline (product owner, asking the bank).
Ranked drivers: (1) verifiable for many years, even after the certificate has ended (KS-1, KS-2); (2) a leaked key's damage limited in time (KS-3); (3) no key outside an HSM (KS-4).

A signature over a document's bytes does not by itself show when it was made (InvoiceSigning signs only the data bytes); a date written inside the document is no proof, since whoever holds a leaked key can sign a document with any date in it.
claims.source_hint: samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Security/InvoiceSigning.cs @ stage-4 (ECDsa SignData over bytes); .NET API docs ECDsa.SignData

claims.text: ADR 0015: losing the HSM loses the key; Đơn Hàng then creates a new key, gets a new certificate, and invoices already signed stay checkable with the old certificate.

ADR 0023 lists reopen conditions; the first: a contract demanding the key in an HSM on Đơn Hàng's or the customer's own machines, then a new ADR replaces 0023 for that key only, other keys unchanged. The second (leaving ADR 0022's provider) is not one of the bank's assumptions.
TT-3 (invoice key does not leave the key protection device) is decided in ADRs 0015/0023: the provider's HSM service, only Payments' ServiceAccount may sign; no HSM exists yet at stage-4.

Prerequisites: a verifier follows the chain to a trusted root and InvoiceCertificates trusts only Đơn Hàng's own root; compliance-controls.md maps TT-1..TT-7 to control, evidence, gap; leaving the provider of ADR 0023 means a new key and certificate.
claims.source_hint: five-line summaries of backend.l4.pki-and-signing, management.l4.compliance-controls, k8s.l4.keys-stay-in-the-key-service

claims.text: ADR 0022 chose managed Kubernetes and reopens on a contract demanding a customer's own machines; ADR 0029 names an own-machine key contract as a reopen condition of both 0022 and 0023, so if the third assumption fails the team checks 0022 and updates that assumption.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0022-production-tren-kubernetes-managed.md Điều kiện mở lại (line 78); docs/adr/0029 lines 61-62; docs/adr/0023 lines 45-49 @ stage-4

claims.text: Framing trade-offs: signing only as an invoice cannot meet KS-2/KS-3; letting the bank ask Đơn Hàng breaks KS-1 and binds Đơn Hàng to answer for ten years; ranking time first fits when a third party checks long after signing.

Because statements may wait hours, the design may add signing steps that are slow or wait on another party, at the price that a month's statements depend on those steps working before the bank's deadline, a risk later steps must name.

Choices: twenty years changes KS-2's measure, not the driver; a contract demanding own-machine HSM meets ADR 0023's first reopen condition and changes neither scenarios nor drivers; signing down for a day near the deadline is a risk with an owner, not a load change.

A certificate's end date limits when signatures may be made under it; a signature made inside the validity period can still be accepted later if the verifier can show when it was made, and a check against today's date shows the certificate as ended.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/bank-signing-requirements.md KS-2 line 27; .NET API docs X509ChainPolicy.VerificationTime

claims.text: Checking a signed statement years later needs more than the signature: the certificate, a chain to a root the verifier trusts, and proof the certificate was neither ended nor revoked at signing time, since validity is judged at the time of signing.
claims.source_hint: .NET API docs X509ChainPolicy.VerificationTime remarks (signature must have been valid at the time of signing); InvoiceCertificates.IsTrusted @ stage-4 (CustomRootTrust)
